title: Privacy ledger for analytics derivatives and compliance replay
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Console analytics produces a range of derived artifacts (aggregates, sampled exports, and troubleshoot replays) that can indirectly contain or be linked to PII. Existing deletion and scrubbing pipelines target raw event streams, but there is no reliable, auditable ledger mapping derivative artifacts back to the original consent and retention state. Goal: build a lightweight 'privacy ledger' service that records lineage and retention metadata for derived analytics artifacts at create-time, exposes a queryable API for compliance audits, and drives targeted replay/redaction/deletion of derivatives when user consent or retention windows change. This reduces over-deletion risk and enables scoped compliance replays without reprocessing entire historical datasets.
acceptance_criteria: Privacy ledger accepts create/update/delete events for derived artifacts with lineage pointers and retention metadata
API supports lookup by original_event_id, user_id_hash, and artifact_id and returns retention and consent status
Automated job can produce a scoped deletion manifest for downstream systems (dashboards, aggregate exports) from ledger queries
Audit log generated for every ledger-driven replay or redaction action with a linkable run ID
End-to-end integration test demonstrates deletion propagation for a synthetic derived artifact within 24 hours of consent revocation
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Spike completed to evaluate storage options (DynamoDB vs Postgres + JSONB). Chosen Postgres for richer query patterns and transactional guarantees.

2026-02-26: Schema proposal v1 posted to Confluence: includes artifact_id, parent_event_ids (as hashes), user_id_hash, created_at, retention_tier, consent_version, exporter_tag. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Privacy+Ledger+Design
2026-03-01: Implemented prototype service and API contract. Local integration with console-metrics exporter simulated. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1289
2026-03-04: Completed internal privacy review checklist items 1-4. Flagged need for HMAC-based user_id hashing and key rotation support; security to own KMS integration.
Next: wire up ledger-driven deletion worker and add SLO on deletion completion latency
design_decisions: Store canonical lineage in Postgres to support multi-criteria queries and transactional updates; background GC will compact parents older than retention windows.
Persist only hashed identifiers (SHA256 + per-tenant HMAC) for user_id references to avoid storing raw PII in the ledger.
Keep the ledger slim: do not duplicate large aggregates; instead store artifact metadata and pointers to export locations (S3 path, dashboard id).
Use a modular 'replay-driver' interface so different downstream systems (dashboards, exports, analytics backfills) can implement platform-specific redaction handlers.
Prefer eventual consistency for deletion propagation but provide an optional synchronous mode for high-risk customers (configurable in Dedicated/Private deployments).
testing_plan: Unit tests for API validators and hashing; integration tests that simulate consent_revocation workflow and assert that ledger returns correct artifact list; e2e (staging) job that runs deletion_driver and verifies downstream S3 export manifests are marked/removed per retention policy.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal opt-in (10% of console traffic) with dry-run deletion_driver that only emits manifests; Phase 2: enable replay/redaction for non-production namespaces; Phase 3: gated rollout for production customers with compliance opt-in and monitoring (2 weeks between phases).
rollback_plan: If misclassification or over-deletion is observed, pause deletion_driver, restore artifacts from S3 snapshot (we'll keep 7-day tombstone backups for rollbacks), and run forensic query using ledger to enumerate impacted artifacts.
open_risks: Risk: Hash collisions or deterministic linkage might allow re-identification when combined with external datasets. Mitigation: per-tenant HMAC + key rotation + rate limits on lookup API.

Risk: Downstream systems may not implement idempotent redaction handlers leading to partial state. Mitigation: require idempotency in replay-driver contract and add verification step in deletion_driver.
Risk: Large fan-out when revoking high-volume user_id across many derived artifacts. Mitigation: batch and throttle replay jobs, provide emergency fast-path for regulated takedowns.
notes: This ticket coordinates with Data Privacy (legal) for audit requirements and with Platform Security for KMS/HSM integration. We should capture schema migration plan into a separate migration ticket (ENG-716483).
